To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ovarian cancer cell lines express ET-1, ET-3, ETA and ETB receptor mRNAs and that exogenous addition of ET-1 or ET-2 to these cells results in a specific dose-dependent increase in cell number.
endothelin (ET) expression and responsiveness are present in human ovarian carcinoma (OvCa) cells.

(1) human ovarian cancer cell lines express mRNA for ET-1 and ETA- and ETB-receptors, (2) immunoreactive ET-like peptide is secreted by human ovarian cancer cell line, (3) ET-1 and -2, but not ET-3, stimulate growth of human ovarian cancer cell, (4) ETA-R antagonists inhibit growth of ovarian cancer cell, and (5) antisense oligonucleotide to ETA-R inhibits growth of ovarian cancer
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the endothelin family of growth factors in the pathogenesis of human ovarian carcinoma.
the potential role of immunoreactive ETs in the growth regulation of human ovarian carcinoma cell cultures.
the potential role of the endothelins as growth regulators in human ovarian cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ETs are expressed by human ovarian carcinoma cells, that they have specific receptors, and that they can affect growth of the cells in culture.
ET-1 may have a role in autocrine regulation of ovarian carcinoma cell growth in vitro.
ET-1 may act as a growth regulator in ovarian cancer cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ET-1 and its receptors are expressed in human ovarian carcinoma.
ovarian cancer cells express ET-1, ET-2 and ET-3 and have both ETA and ETb receptors.
endothelins are present in human ovarian carcinoma in vitro and may act as autocrine regulators of cell growth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ET-1 can act as a growth factor for ovarian carcinoma cells and this may be mediated through the ETA-receptor.

the expression of ET-1, ET-3, ETA and ETB receptor mRNA in PEO4 cells is consistent with the presence of a single receptor site of high affinity and a second lower affinity binding site in these cells.
the ET system may have a role in the growth regulation of ovarian carcinoma cells.
